{{Short description|American mathematician (born 1953)}}
'''James Wesley Cogdell''' (born 22 September 1953) is an American mathematician.

==Education and career==
He graduated from [[Yale University]] in 1977 with a bachelor's degree and in 1981 with a Ph.D. His doctoral dissertation ''Arithmetic Quotients of the Complex 2-Ball and Modular Forms of Nebentypus'' was supervised by [[Ilya Piatetski-Shapiro]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|name=James Wesley Cogdell|id=30511}}</ref> Cogdell was a postdoc at the [[University of Maryland]] and the [[University of California, Los Angeles]]. He was from 1982 to 1988 an assistant professor at [[Rutgers University]]. At [[Oklahoma State University]] he was from 1987 to 1988 assistant professor, from 1988 to 1994 an associate professor, and from 1994 to 2004 a full professor (from 1999 as Southwestern Bell Professor, from 2000 as Regents Professor, and from 2003 as Vaughan Foundation Professor). In 2004 he became a professor at [[Ohio State University]].<ref name=homepage>{{cite web|title=James W. Cogdell|website=Ohio State University|url=https://people.math.osu.edu/cogdell.1/}} (with online links for many of Cogdell's papers)</ref>

In autumn 1983 and for the academic year 1999–2000 he was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]]. He has held visiting positions at [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], at the [[University of Iowa]], at [[Fields Institute]], and at the [[Erwin Schrödinger International Institute for Mathematical Physics]] (where he gave the 2009 Erwin Schrödinger Lecture).<ref name=homepage/>

Cogdell works on [[L-function]]s, [[automorphic form]]s (within the context of the [[Langlands program]]), and analytic number theory. In collaboration with Piatetski-Shapiro, he proved [[converse theorem]]s for L-functions for the [[general linear group]]s <math>GL_n</math>. The goal is to characterize the L-functions that originate from automorphic forms. For <math>GL_2</math> this was solved by [[Hervé Jacquet]] and [[Robert Langlands]] and for <math>GL_3</math> by Jacquet, Piatetski-Shapiro and [[Joseph Shalika]]. The problem goes back to [[Erich Hecke]]'s characterization of the [[Dirichlet series]] that come from [[modular form]]s.

In 2002 Cogdell was, with Piatetski-Shapiro, an Invited Speaker with talk ''Converse theorems, functoriality and applications to number theory'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Beijing]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Cogdell, J. W.|author2=Piatetski-Shapiro, I. I.|year=2003|title=Converse theorems, functoriality, and applications to number theory|eprint=math/0304230|postscript=; Journal reference: ''Proceedings of the ICM'', Beijing 2002, vol. 2, 119–128}}</ref> He was an editor, with [[Simon Gindikin]] and [[Peter Sarnak]], for ''Selected Works of Ilya Piatetski-Shapiro'' (2000, [[American Mathematical Society|AMS]]).<ref name="Piatetsky-Shapiro2000">{{cite book|author=Piatetski-Shapiro, Ilya|editor=Cogdell, James|editor2=Gindikin, Simon|editor3=Sarnak, Peter|title=Selected Works of Ilya Piatetski-Shapiro|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=q3xSNdApLVEC|year=2000|publisher=American Mathematical Soc.|isbn=978-0-8218-0930-3}}</ref>

Cogdell was elected in 2012 a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|website=ams.org|url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_inst.cgi}}</ref> and in 2016 a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Historic Fellows|website=American Association for the Advancement of Science|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic}}</ref>
